# III. Building the workflow {.unnumbered}

A useful data product rarely stops at one input table. This part adds reusable preparation, execution semantics, persistence, and dependencies between products.

The sequence matters. First make transformations explicit. Then understand what `dr_run()`, `dr_collect()`, and `dr_publish()` mean. Only after that choose a storage boundary. Finally compose multiple products so their dependencies become part of the graph rather than hidden setup code.

::: {.callout-note title="By the end of this part"}
You should be able to build a small product graph, run it without writing, publish an accepted result, and explain which parts of the workflow are logical definitions and which parts are physical execution choices.
:::
